records.jp: この辺りまで来ると、人もいないし<CR>結構静かだよね
records.en_original: It sure is quiet. I guess not many people come out all the way here.
records.en_auxiliary: It sure is quiet. I guess not many people come out all the way here.
records.en: Not many people come this far,<CR>so it's pretty quiet.

records.jp: うん。<CR>きららは、静かな場所が好き
records.en_original: Indeed. I prefer the quiet.
records.en_auxiliary: Indeed. I prefer the quiet.
records.en: Yeah.<CR>Kirara likes quiet places.

records.jp: 石灯籠といえばさー<CR>こんな怖い話があるんだけど……
records.en_original: These stone lanterns kinda remind me of a spooky story I know...
records.en_auxiliary: These stone lanterns kinda remind me of a spooky story I know...
records.en: These stone lanterns kinda<CR>remind me of a spooky story I know...

records.jp: ……ということで、その石灯籠を壊したせいで<CR>男は右腕を失うことになっちゃったんだって
records.en_original: ...And as punishment for breaking the lantern, he lost his right arm forever!
records.en_auxiliary: ...And as punishment for breaking the lantern, he lost his right arm forever!
records.en: ...And because the man broke that stone lantern,<CR>he ended up losing his right arm.

records.jp: 因果応報というやつだな
records.en_original: Divine retribution, was it?
records.en_auxiliary: Divine retribution, was it?
records.en: That is what they call karmic retribution.

records.jp: 古い物には魂が宿るって言うし、<CR>この石灯籠も大事にしないとだよねー
records.en_original: They say that souls rest in old things, after all. Gotta make sure we take care of these stone lanterns!
records.en_auxiliary: They say that souls rest in old things, after all. Gotta make sure we take care of these stone lanterns!
records.en: They say souls dwell in old objects,<CR>so we need to take care of this stone lantern too.

records.jp: 石灯籠か……<CR>そういえば、きららも……
records.en_original: Yes... That reminds me of something as well.
records.en_auxiliary: Yes... That reminds me of something as well.
records.en: A stone lantern...<CR>Come to think of it, Kirara also...

records.jp: おや、もしかしてきららさんも<CR>石灯籠にまつわる怖い話をお持ちですかな？
records.en_original: Oho? Do you have a scary story about stone lanterns too, Kirara?
records.en_auxiliary: Oho? Do you have a scary story about stone lanterns too, Kirara?
records.en: Oh?<CR>Could Kirara-san also have a scary story involving a stone lantern?

records.jp: ううん。<CR>怖い話じゃないけど……いい？
records.en_original: Not quite. May I still tell you about it?
records.en_auxiliary: Not quite. May I still tell you about it?
records.en: Not quite.<CR>May I still tell you about it?

records.jp: うん、もちろんいいよ
records.en_original: Of course!
records.en_auxiliary: Of course!
records.en: Of course!

records.jp: きららの話、いろいろ聞いてみたいし
records.en_original: I'm always interested in what you have to say, Kirara.
records.en_auxiliary: I'm always interested in what you have to say, Kirara.
records.en: I want to hear all sorts of stories from you, Kirara.

records.jp: そう言われると……なんかプレッシャー。<CR>やっぱり、やめる
records.en_original: That...is a lot of pressure. I've changed my mind.
records.en_auxiliary: That...is a lot of pressure. I've changed my mind.
records.en: When you say that... Kirara feels pressured.<CR>She will not tell it after all.

records.jp: ええ！？　やめないで！
records.en_original: Wait, no don't!
records.en_auxiliary: Wait, no don't!
records.en: Wait, no don't!

records.jp: ふむ……そこまで言うなら、仕方ない。<CR>聞かせてしんぜよう
records.en_original: Hmph... Very well. If you are so desperate to hear, let me regale you.
records.en_auxiliary: Hmph... Very well. If you are so desperate to hear, let me regale you.
records.en: Hm... If you insist, very well.<CR>Kirara shall grant you the privilege of hearing it.

records.jp: ありがたき幸せ！
records.en_original: Thank you, oh great one!
records.en_auxiliary: Thank you, oh great one!
records.en: Thank you, oh great one!

records.jp: 怖い話が良かったなあ……
records.en_original: Aw... I wanted to hear a scary story.
records.en_auxiliary: Aw... I wanted to hear a scary story.
records.en: Aw... I wanted to hear a scary story.

records.jp: 次回までには、ストックしておく。<CR>……５本ぐらい
records.en_original: I'll make sure I have plenty for next time then. Is five enough?
records.en_auxiliary: I'll make sure I have plenty for next time then. Is five enough?
records.en: Kirara will stock about<CR>five for next time.

records.jp: さすがです、きらら様
records.en_original: More than enough! That's my Kirara!
records.en_auxiliary: More than enough! That's my Kirara!
records.en: As expected of Kirara-sama.

records.jp: どやあ
records.en_original: Heh.
records.en_auxiliary: Heh.
records.en: Heh.

records.jp: それで、きららの石灯籠の話って？
records.en_original: So what's the story about?
records.en_auxiliary: So what's the story about?
records.en: So what's the story about?

records.jp: ん～……きらら、子どもの頃は<CR>石灯籠の明かりを見るのが好きだったなって
records.en_original: Let's see here... When I was a little girl, I loved watching the lanterns glow in the night.
records.en_auxiliary: Let's see here... When I was a little girl, I loved watching the lanterns glow in the night.
records.en: Hmm... When Kirara was a child,<CR>she liked watching the light from stone lanterns.

records.jp: へー。<CR>家の近くに灯籠があったとか？
records.en_original: You had some near your house?
records.en_auxiliary: You had some near your house?
records.en: You had some<CR>near your house?

records.jp: ん、そんな感じ。お祭りごとがあると<CR>石灯籠に灯りがついてた
records.en_original: Something like that. They would always be lit during special events like festivals.
records.en_auxiliary: Something like that. They would always be lit during special events like festivals.
records.en: Something like that. When there was a festival<CR>or ceremony, the stone lanterns would be lit.

records.jp: ゆっくりと瞬くみたいに揺れる<CR>ろうそくの灯りが、綺麗だったのだ
records.en_original: The flickering glow of the candles were beautiful.
records.en_auxiliary: The flickering glow of the candles were beautiful.
records.en: The candlelight swaying as though<CR>it slowly blinked was beautiful.

records.jp: 私、石灯籠ってあんまりなじみが<CR>なかったんだけど、実際に見ると……
records.en_original: I never really got the chance to see many stone lanterns growing up, but now that I've seen them up close...
records.en_auxiliary: I never really got the chance to see many stone lanterns growing up, but now that I've seen them up close...
records.en: I wasn't very familiar with stone lanterns,<CR>but seeing one in person...

records.jp: そんなに怖くないよね
records.en_original: They're not scary at all, are they?
records.en_auxiliary: They're not scary at all, are they?
records.en: They're not scary at all, are they?

records.jp: 愛央は、怖い話に影響されすぎだ
records.en_original: I think you put too much stock into that story, Ao.
records.en_auxiliary: I think you put too much stock into that story, Ao.
records.en: Ao is too influenced by scary stories.

records.jp: 石灯籠の役目は、道を照らすこと。<CR>怪談とは関係ない
records.en_original: Lanterns are meant to guide travelers on dark roads. They're not supposed to be scary.
records.en_auxiliary: Lanterns are meant to guide travelers on dark roads. They're not supposed to be scary.
records.en: The purpose of a stone lantern is to illuminate the road.<CR>It has nothing to do with ghost stories.

records.jp: あはは、やっぱり？
records.en_original: Ahaha, I guess that makes sense.
records.en_auxiliary: Ahaha, I guess that makes sense.
records.en: Ahaha, I guess that makes sense.

records.jp: 石灯籠のこの穴から、オバケが出てくる話とかも<CR>あるんだけどさ、結構小さいんだねー
records.en_original: There are stories about ghosts and stuff coming out through this hole, but its pretty teensy, huh?
records.en_auxiliary: There are stories about ghosts and stuff coming out through this hole, but its pretty teensy, huh?
records.en: There are stories about ghosts coming out through this opening,<CR>but it's actually pretty small.

records.jp: 穴……火口のことか
records.en_original: Hole? Ah, the fire box?
records.en_auxiliary: Hole? Ah, the fire box?
records.en: Opening... You mean the higuchi.

records.jp: へぇ！<CR>この穴、火口っていうんだ
records.en_original: Is that what it's called? You learn something new every day!
records.en_auxiliary: Is that what it's called? You learn something new every day!
records.en: Oh!<CR>This opening is called a higuchi.

records.jp: 面白いデザインだよね。<CR>なんか、すっごく和って感じだし！
records.en_original: They really have a cool design, don't they? They're like, quintessentially Japanese!
records.en_auxiliary: They really have a cool design, don't they? They're like, quintessentially Japanese!
records.en: They really have a cool design, don't they?<CR>They're like, quintessentially Japanese!

records.jp: うん。この灯籠は、受花と格狭間の装飾が<CR>細かくてよくできている
records.en_original: Quite. Not only that, if you look closely, you can see the intricate designs on the upper support and in between the gaps.
records.en_auxiliary: Quite. Not only that, if you look closely, you can see the intricate designs on the upper support and in between the gaps.
records.en: Yes. The ukebana and kouzama ornamentation on this lantern is intricate<CR>and skillfully made.

records.en_original: ...What?
records.en_auxiliary: ...What?
records.en: ...What?

records.jp: 笠の広がりも上品で、火袋の造りにも<CR>力強さを感じる
records.en_original: The way the roof curves out gives it quite a sophisticated feeling. The fire box also has a certain appeal to it.
records.en_auxiliary: The way the roof curves out gives it quite a sophisticated feeling. The fire box also has a certain appeal to it.
records.en: The elegant spread of the roof and the construction of the hibukuro<CR>also convey strength.

records.jp: ちょ、待って！　そこまで、本格的に<CR>デザインについては分析してない！
records.en_original: Just a sec, Kirara! I didn't expect a full breakdown of its artistic worth!
records.en_auxiliary: Just a sec, Kirara! I didn't expect a full breakdown of its artistic worth!
records.en: Wait!<CR>I wasn't analyzing its design that seriously!

records.jp: そうなのか？
records.en_original: You didn't?
records.en_auxiliary: You didn't?
records.en: You didn't?

records.jp: そうなの！　てか、きらら。<CR>石灯籠についても詳しいとか何者……
records.en_original: Of course not! But, I didn't realize you were so clued in on lanterns, Kirara.
records.en_auxiliary: Of course not! But, I didn't realize you were so clued in on lanterns, Kirara.
records.en: That's right!<CR>But Kirara, how do you even know so much about stone lanterns...?

records.jp: 普通に生活していたら得られる知識では
records.en_original: It's simple common knowledge, isn't it?
records.en_auxiliary: It's simple common knowledge, isn't it?
records.en: You'd pick that up just from everyday life.

records.jp: いや、無理でしょ！　火袋だけは<CR>なんとなーく、聞いたことあったけど
records.en_original: No way! I mean, I think I'd heard of fire box before...
records.en_auxiliary: No way! I mean, I think I'd heard of fire box before...
records.en: No way!<CR>I had only vaguely heard the word hibukuro before.

records.jp: ……確か、この火を灯すところを<CR>火袋って言うんだよね
records.en_original: It's the place where the candle goes, right?
records.en_auxiliary: It's the place where the candle goes, right?
records.en: ...This part where the flame is lit is called the hibukuro,<CR>right?

records.jp: うん。ここが火袋。で、この穴が火口。
records.en_original: Indeed. And the window allows you to access it.
records.en_auxiliary: Indeed. And the window allows you to access it.
records.en: Yes. This is the hibukuro. And this opening is the higuchi.

records.jp: あ……火口で怖い話を思い出した
records.en_original: Ah! Windows reminded me of another scary story.
records.en_auxiliary: Ah! Windows reminded me of another scary story.
records.en: Ah... The higuchi reminded Kirara of a frightening story.

records.jp: え、なになに？
records.en_original: Ooh! I'm all ears!
records.en_auxiliary: Ooh! I'm all ears!
records.en: Ooh! I'm all ears!

records.jp: 子供の頃、石灯籠の火口に腕を入れたら<CR>抜けなくなったことがあった
records.en_original: When I was but a girl, I put my arm inside the window of a lantern...and it got stuck.
records.en_auxiliary: When I was but a girl, I put my arm inside the window of a lantern...and it got stuck.
records.en: When Kirara was a child, she put her arm through a stone lantern's higuchi<CR>and could not pull it back out.

records.jp: あー、なんか子供がやりそうな悪戯だね
records.en_original: Oops. I can imagine most kids would try that at least once.
records.en_auxiliary: Oops. I can imagine most kids would try that at least once.
records.en: Oops. I can imagine most kids would try that at least once.

records.jp: どんなに引っ張っても抜けなくて……<CR>気が付けば、辺りはとっぷりと日が暮れて……
records.en_original: No matter how hard I pulled, it just wouldn't come loose. Soon enough, night started to fall...
records.en_auxiliary: No matter how hard I pulled, it just wouldn't come loose. Soon enough, night started to fall...
records.en: No matter how hard I pulled, it just wouldn't come loose.<CR>Soon enough, night started to fall...

records.jp: えっ、そんなに！？
records.en_original: You were stuck for that long?!
records.en_auxiliary: You were stuck for that long?!
records.en: You were stuck for that long?!

records.jp: 最終的に、大人たちが、チェンソーとか、<CR>ドリルとか持って来て……
records.en_original: Eventually, some of the adults had to free me with hammers and a drill.
records.en_auxiliary: Eventually, some of the adults had to free me with hammers and a drill.
records.en: Eventually, the adults came with a chainsaw, a drill,<CR>and other tools...

records.jp: うっわ……想像したら、ゾッとした。<CR>それは、ガチで怖い……
records.en_original: Whoa, that IS scary...
records.en_auxiliary: Whoa, that IS scary...
records.en: Whoa,<CR>that IS scary...

records.jp: うん。<CR>今思い出しても、あれは怖かった
records.en_original: Yes. Even the memory is still rather unsettling.
records.en_auxiliary: Yes. Even the memory is still rather unsettling.
records.en: Yes.<CR>Even the memory is still rather unsettling.

records.jp: それでよく石灯籠が好きって言えたね
records.en_original: But you said you liked stone lanterns though, right? Even after all that?
records.en_auxiliary: But you said you liked stone lanterns though, right? Even after all that?
records.en: But you said you liked stone lanterns though, right? Even after all that?

records.jp: 石灯籠に罪はない。<CR>悪いのは、腕を突っ込んでしまったきらら
records.en_original: The lantern did nothing wrong. I was the one who stuck my arm in.
records.en_auxiliary: The lantern did nothing wrong. I was the one who stuck my arm in.
records.en: The stone lantern was not at fault.<CR>Kirara was at fault for putting her arm inside.

records.jp: でも、今でも石灯籠をみると<CR>不思議と、あの穴に腕を入れたく……
records.en_original: Although, saying that, for some reason my arm feels drawn to that lantern's window...
records.en_auxiliary: Although, saying that, for some reason my arm feels drawn to that lantern's window...
records.en: But even now, when Kirara sees a stone lantern,<CR>she strangely feels like putting her arm through that opening...

records.jp: わー！　ダメダメ！！
records.en_original: Whoa, hold it, Kirara!
records.en_auxiliary: Whoa, hold it, Kirara!
records.en: Whoa, hold it, Kirara!

records.jp: 穴があったら入れたくなる心理とは、<CR>まさにこのことか
records.en_original: I suppose what they say is true, people are inexplicably drawn to stick their arms into any welcoming opening.
records.en_auxiliary: I suppose what they say is true, people are inexplicably drawn to stick their arms into any welcoming opening.
records.en: So this is the psychology of wanting to put something in whenever<CR>there is a hole.

records.jp: いや、絶対に違う！<CR>てか、なんの話！？
records.en_original: Wait, no, who says that?!
records.en_auxiliary: Wait, no, who says that?!
records.en: Wait,<CR>no, who says that?!

records.jp: いやー、私だったらトラウマになるかも。<CR>チェンソーは、やばいって。チェンソーは
records.en_original: Whew, if it was me, I'd be super traumatized. What if they had to use a chain saw to remove my arm?
records.en_auxiliary: Whew, if it was me, I'd be super traumatized. What if they had to use a chain saw to remove my arm?
records.en: That might traumatize me. A chainsaw is too much.<CR>Seriously, a chainsaw.

records.jp: うむ、チェンソーはやばい。<CR>……ん？　チェンソー……？
records.en_original: Quite, a chainsaw would certainly hurt... Wait... Saw...? Saw...?
records.en_auxiliary: Quite, a chainsaw would certainly hurt... Wait... Saw...? Saw...?
records.en: Indeed, chainsaws are nasty.<CR>...Hm? Chainsaw...?

records.jp: どうしたの？
records.en_original: Is something the matter?
records.en_auxiliary: Is something the matter?
records.en: Is something the matter?

records.jp: 今、唐突にあれが食べたくなった
records.en_original: All of a sudden I'm really hungry.
records.en_auxiliary: All of a sudden I'm really hungry.
records.en: Kirara suddenly wants to eat that.

records.jp: ピリッと辛いソーセージ
records.en_original: I want some super spicy sausages.
records.en_auxiliary: I want some super spicy sausages.
records.en: A spicy sausage.

records.jp: ……もしかして、チョリソー？
records.en_original: Why? Oh, wait... Saw...sage? Sausage? Is THAT why?
records.en_auxiliary: Why? Oh, wait... Saw...sage? Sausage? Is THAT why?
records.en: ...Do you mean chorizo?

records.jp: おお、それだ！
records.en_original: Exactly!
records.en_auxiliary: Exactly!
records.en: Exactly!

records.jp: フラグメント「<CLGR>%s<CLNR>」を<CR>手に入れました
records.en_original: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR> Fragment.
records.en_auxiliary: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR> Fragment.
records.en: Obtained <CLGR>%s<CLNR><CR>Fragment.
